'''''Eleocharis acicularis''''' is a species of [[Eleocharis|spikesedge]] known by the common names '''needle spikerush'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ELAC|taxon=Eleocharis acicularis|accessdate=18 January 2016}}</ref> and '''least spikerush'''. It is widespread across [[Europe]], central and southeastern [[Asia]], [[North America]] and northeastern [[South America]] as far south as [[Ecuador]].<ref name="wcsp">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=242255 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> It is also found in [[Australia]], where it is probably an [[introduced species]].<ref name="lippi">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242357729 Flora of North America, Vol. 23 Page 108, ''Eleocharis acicularis'' (Linnaeus) Roemer & Schultes in J. J. Roemer et al., Syst. Veg. 2: 154. 1817.]</ref>

''Eleocharis acicularis'' is an annual or perennial spikesedge with long, grasslike stems to about 15 centimeters (6 inches) in height, shorter in [[bog]] conditions, from a creeping [[rhizome]]. In shallow water it will form short spikes of tiny flowers amongst flat overlapping [[bract]]s. The tiny flowers are less than five millimeters in diameter and are borne at the tip of each stem in single, sharply pointed, lanceoloid [[Raceme|spikelets]] up to about six millimeters long. This is a plant of marshes, [[vernal pool]]s, and bogs.<ref name="lippi" />

''Eleocharis acicularis'' is sold commercially as an [[aquascape]] plant suitable for inclusion in artificial aquatic environments. It thrives with plenty of light and a high concentration of [[carbon dioxide]].<ref>Roe, Colin D. (1967), ''A Manual of Aquarium Plants'', Shirley Aquatics, Solihull</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aquascapingworld.com/plantpedia/full_view_plant.php?item_id=46&plant=Eleocharis%20acicularis |title=Aquascaping World Plantpedia, ''Eleocharis acicularis'' |access-date=2014-07-25 |archive-date=2014-07-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728202331/http://www.aquascapingworld.com/plantpedia/full_view_plant.php?item_id=46&plant=Eleocharis%20acicularis |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]], {{lang|la|acicularis}}, is derived from [[Latin]] and means "needle-shaped".<ref name="Eggli Newton 2004">{{cite book |last=Eggli |first=Urs |last2=Newton |first2=Leonard E. |title=Etymological Dictionary of Succulent Plant Names |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |year=2004 |isbn=978-3-540-00489-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=u2n5vusQ1DEC&pg=PA1 |access-date=14 November 2018 |page=1}}</ref>

== Varieties ==
Two varieties are recognized:<ref name="wcsp" />

* ''Eleocharis acicularis'' var. ''acicularis'' – most of species range
* ''Eleocharis acicularis'' var. ''porcata'' <small>S.G.Sm.</small> – western North America from Alberta south to New Mexico and Louisiana
